stories.body: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due to visit Moscow on Saturday and Kyiv on Sunday carrying what President Donald Trump described as a proposal to end the war in Ukraine. The meetings would be their first reported visit to Ukraine after several trips to Russia. President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would meet the envoys and called for both sides to ensure the safety of their airspace during the visits. Although Putin said a deal may be possible, Russia continues to demand territorial concessions that Kyiv and its European partners reject.
stories.headline: Trump sends envoys to Moscow and Kyiv with a new Ukraine peace proposal

stories.body: A Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security service in central Kyiv, apparently targeting the office used by agency chief Oleksandr Poklad. Zelensky said he had spoken with Poklad and ordered an appropriate, tangible response, while Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha called the attack a major escalation. At least five people were reported injured, nearby businesses were damaged, and emergency crews cordoned off the area. The rare successful hit on a central government building comes amid intensified Russian drone attacks and ahead of the planned US mediation visit.
stories.headline: Russian drone strike hits Ukraine's security-service headquarters in Kyiv

stories.body: Explosions of unknown origin were reported near Iran's Kharg Island in the Gulf, home to a crucial oil-export terminal. Iranian media also carried unconfirmed reports that a tanker near the island had been hit by missiles fired by US forces. The reports emerged during the continuing regional war and have not been independently confirmed.
stories.headline: Explosions reported near Iran's key Kharg Island oil terminal

stories.body: At least two people were confirmed dead and dozens injured after two explosions at a military barracks in Viacha, about 30 kilometres from La Paz. Authorities said pyrotechnic material and fireworks were stored at the site, while local health officials put the likely death toll as high as 10 to 15 and said seven people remained missing. Dozens of nearby homes were damaged, and firefighters warned residents to stay at least 150 metres away because of the risk of another blast. An investigation is under way into the cause and storage of the material.
stories.headline: Deadly blasts strike a Bolivian military barracks

stories.body: The UN General Assembly voted 164 to 1, with six abstentions, to encourage a shift away from the Mercator projection toward maps that more accurately show continental areas, including the Equal Earth projection. The resolution, sponsored by Togo and backed by African Union members, notes that Mercator makes regions near the equator appear smaller while enlarging high-latitude areas; Africa is shown at roughly Greenland's size despite being about 14 times larger. The non-binding measure will not compel governments or institutions to change maps, but supporters expect it to influence education and official use. The United States was the sole vote against.
stories.headline: UN votes to replace Mercator map with a projection showing Africa's true scale

stories.body: Nepal's flood death toll has risen to 1,344, with 4,886 people still missing, according to the latest police figures. Nearly 8,000 personnel remain deployed for search and rescue operations, which have helped almost 9,000 people. Two workers were pulled alive from a hydropower tunnel after being trapped for about 10 days; one was reported in critical condition with severe hypothermia. Authorities face a major challenge identifying victims, with most recovered bodies still unidentified and DNA samples being collected.
stories.headline: Nepal flood death toll rises above 1,300 as rescue operations continue

stories.body: North Carolina has begun sending ballots for the November midterm elections as the Trump administration asks the Supreme Court to allow new Postal Service rules for mail ballots to take effect. The rules would require states to provide voter lists and use approved ballot-envelope designs, with the Postal Service able to refuse delivery for noncompliance. Current and former election officials from both parties say changes of that scale cannot be implemented so close to the election, because ballots and envelopes are already printed and local systems are in place. The policy remains blocked by a federal judge while the legal challenge continues.
stories.headline: Election officials say it is too late to implement Trump's proposed mail-ballot rules

stories.body: ICE officer Christian Castro was released on a $75,000 unsecured bond and ordered to wear a GPS monitor after appearing in federal court on charges that he lied to investigators about a January shooting in Minnesota. Prosecutors allege he falsely claimed he had been attacked with a broom and shovel before he shot Venezuelan man Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis in the leg. The indictment says Castro fired through a front door while standing as Sosa-Celis and another man were retreating inside. Castro plans to plead not guilty and is due in federal court in Minnesota on September 18.
stories.headline: ICE officer charged with lying about Minnesota shooting is released on bond

stories.body: A Lancaster County coroner has confirmed that a six-week-old infant died of measles at home on August 18. The child had been receiving palliative care at home shortly after birth. The death comes as Pennsylvania public-health workers continue efforts to contain the state's growing measles outbreak through local immunisation clinics and outreach.
stories.headline: Pennsylvania coroner confirms an infant died of measles amid an ongoing outbreak

stories.body: The average US diesel price reached a record $5.85 a gallon on Friday as the war with Iran disrupts global fuel supplies. Since diesel powers freight trucks, trains, ships and farm equipment, the increase is expected to raise the cost of transporting a broad range of goods, from food to furniture and clothing. Some businesses have already added delivery fees, while higher costs may increasingly appear on store shelves. Regular gasoline averaged $4.15 a gallon, up from $3.20 a year earlier.
stories.headline: US diesel prices reach a record high, raising transport costs

stories.body: Spain's National Court prosecutors have supported opening an investigation into the mass crossing into Ceuta from Morocco in late July, which involved around 80,000 people and left 82 people dead, according to reports. The prosecution argues that the court has jurisdiction because alleged planning occurred in Morocco while the main effects occurred in Spanish territory. Potential offences include facilitating irregular immigration, reckless homicide and injury, and criminal organisation. Prosecutors have requested partial secrecy for the case, and Judge María Tardón is expected to decide next week whether to proceed.
stories.headline: Prosecutors back a National Court investigation into the Ceuta migration crisis

stories.body: Spain's Fiscal and Financial Policy Council approved the first stage of a new regional-financing model that the government says would add about €21 billion annually for regions in the common system from 2027. Only Catalonia and the Canary Islands backed the proposal alongside the Finance Ministry; the other regions voting opposed it, including PP-led governments and the Socialist governments of Asturias and Castilla-La Mancha, while Madrid boycotted the meeting. The government says every region would receive more resources and financing gaps would narrow, but critics say the model was negotiated first with Catalonia and undermines territorial equality. The voluntary model must now go to the cabinet and then face a difficult vote in Congress.
stories.headline: Spain approves a new regional-financing model despite broad opposition

stories.body: Spain's weather agency, Aemet, has warned of extreme wildfire risk across broad areas of the peninsula, particularly the centre, northeast, Ebro valley, eastern interior and much of the south. Persistently high temperatures, low humidity and conditions favourable to rapid fire spread are expected to continue, with orange heat alerts in parts of Aragón and Catalonia where temperatures could reach 39C. The Canary Islands have also issued wildfire alerts for areas of Tenerife and Gran Canaria as a tropical-style warm episode brings heat, wind and low humidity.
stories.headline: Spain faces extreme wildfire risk as exceptional September heat continues

stories.body: Volkswagen says no decision has been made on the future of the Seat brand after 2030, with its continuation dependent on regulation, consumer demand and market conditions. The company said the difficulty and cost of developing electric models make further investment in Seat increasingly complex, though planned updates including mild-hybrid versions of the Ibiza and Arona will continue. Volkswagen nevertheless reaffirmed its long-term commitment to Seat S.A., Catalonia and Spain, and said Martorell's future is secure as it prepares electric production including the Cupra Raval and Volkswagen ID. Polo.
stories.headline: Volkswagen does not guarantee the Seat brand beyond 2030, though Martorell production remains backed

stories.body: Barcelona's Fabra Observatory recorded 34.1C to 34.2C, setting a new September high in records dating to 1914 and surpassing the previous mark set just two days earlier. Catalonia's Civil Protection agency has activated an intense-heat alert for the weekend, with temperatures forecast to reach 40C in some inland and Ebro Valley areas. Vinebre reached 42.5C, and 77 of 128 long-running weather stations set September records. Authorities are urging protection for vulnerable people and warning of elevated to extreme wildfire risk across parts of the region.
stories.headline: Barcelona records a September temperature record as Catalonia enters an intense heatwave

stories.body: The Metges de Catalunya union says it will intensify protests this autumn unless the Health Department opens negotiations over doctors' working conditions. Its "Not one more minute" campaign, launched in June, urges doctors not to undertake planned voluntary work outside their contracted hours and on-call shifts. The union says the action is already affecting patient care, with waiting lists rising and non-urgent operations no longer carried out after hours. In Girona, surgical activity fell 9.9% in July from a year earlier while the number of people waiting for surgery rose by 578 in one month.
stories.headline: Catalan doctors threaten more protests as campaign against unpaid extra work disrupts care

stories.body: Several Barcelona schools have said their management teams will not join a teachers' strike planned for September 8, the first day of the school year, in order to minimise disruption for pupils and families. The schools say they support the education sector's demands and may participate in future action, but stress that striking remains an individual right and some classes could still be affected. The stoppage remains in place after a final meeting between the USTEC and CGT unions and Education Minister Esther Niubó ended without agreement.
stories.headline: Schools in Barcelona split over teachers' strike planned for the first day of term
